title: You keep saying you’re not ready.
paragraphs: You keep saying you’re not ready.
But what if that’s the very thing keeping you from God’s assignment?
“I am too young.”

That wasn’t just Jeremiah’s line.
That’s ours.
And here’s the tension you don’t want to face:

Is it really humility…
or is it fear wearing a holy mask?

Because it sounds right.
It feels safe.
It even looks spiritual.
But deep down, it’s resistance.

You feel the nudge.
You hear the call.
You know God is asking something of you.
And yet…
You shrink back.

“I’m not ready.”
“I’ll fail.”
“I’m not like them.”
“I don’t know enough Scripture.”
“I still struggle with sin.”
So you step away.

Not because God is silent—
but because His voice is louder than your comfort.
Let’s be honest.
Some of us are not waiting on God.
We are hiding from Him.

Hiding behind excuses.
Hiding behind insecurity.
Hiding behind a version of “humility” that keeps us disobedient.
Jeremiah tried it.
“Ah, Lord God! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth.” (Jeremiah 1:6)
That sounds reasonable.
But God didn’t affirm it.
God confronted it.
“Do not say, ‘I am only a youth’… Do not be afraid… for I am with you.” (Jeremiah 1:7–8)
Did you catch that?

God didn’t argue about Jeremiah’s weakness.
He commanded him to stop declaring it as an excuse.
Because the issue was never Jeremiah’s age.
It was his trust.
And this is where it cuts deep.
You think your limitation disqualifies you.
But God says your limitation is exactly where His power shows up.
“But he said to me, ‘My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.’” (2 Corinthians 12:9)
So what are you really saying when you keep repeating your excuse?

“I’m too young.”
“I’m too broken.”
“I’m too inconsistent.”
“I’ve messed up too much.”
If we’re honest…

We are saying:
“God, what You’ve given me is not enough.”
That’s not humility.
That’s unbelief.
And before you feel condemned—listen carefully.
This is where grace walks in.

Because your biggest issue is not your age.
Not your weakness.
Not even your fear.
It’s sin.
“All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)

Sin bends us inward.
It makes us trust ourselves more than God.
It makes us hide instead of obey.
That’s why we hesitate.
That’s why we resist.
That’s why we keep saying, “Not yet.”
But God didn’t wait for you to be ready.
He came for you while you were still broken.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Let that sink in.
Jesus did not die for a “ready” version of you.

He died for the fearful you.
The insecure you.
The excuse-making you.
The you who keeps saying, “I can’t.”
And on the cross, He didn’t just forgive your sin.
He broke the power of it.
So now, through Christ:

You are not defined by your past.
You are not trapped by your weakness.
You are not disqualified by your fear.
You are called.
“Whoever comes to me I will never cast out.” (John 6:37)
And more than that—
You are sent.
Jesus said, “You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you…” (John 15:16)
Appointed.
Not because you were ready.
But because He is.
So here’s the question you can’t avoid anymore:

Will you keep announcing your excuse…
or will you start trusting His voice?
Because one will keep you stuck.
The other will set you on fire.
You don’t need to feel ready.
You need to repent.

Repent of the unbelief.
Repent of the hiding.
Repent of making your weakness louder than God’s Word.
And then—
Believe.

Believe that Jesus is enough.
Believe that His grace covers you.
Believe that His Spirit empowers you.
Walk trembling if you must.
But walk.
Because delayed obedience is still disobedience.
And your “not yet” might be the very thing delaying someone else’s breakthrough.
Let that hit you.
God didn’t call a perfect Jeremiah.
He called a willing one.
So stop waiting to become someone else.
Surrender who you are—right now—to Christ.
He knows your weakness.
And He chose you anyway.
If this hit your heart…
